subject: On-prem pricing: flat-fee to consumption swap proposal
messages:
From: Jason Li <jason.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem inquiry — can we swap to consumption for pilot?

Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme liked the latency and the deterministic routing. We have one commercial ask before we get to procurement: our CFO is pushing back on committing a large multi-year flat license for the pilot. They asked whether we can start with a short on-prem pilot on a capped consumption model (per-token/host-hour) and then convert to a longer-term flat license if the pilot exceeds thresholds.

Specifics they proposed:
- Pilot duration: 6 months
- Spend cap: $75k (we cover all infra and Redwood platform fee within that cap)
- Conversion: if usage > X tokens or sustained throughput > Y nodes, apply a credit towards a 1- or 2-year on-prem license

Is that something Redwood would entertain? If so we need a sketch of the conversion credit math and a short SOW we can send to legal.

Jason
VP, Infrastructure
Acme Health

[Attachment: pilot_requirements_summary.pdf (1 page)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Jason Li <jason.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem inquiry — can we swap to consumption for pilot?

Jason — thanks, glad the demo hit the mark. Short answer: yes, we can structure a capped consumption pilot with a conversion credit. I want to loop in Marissa (pricing) and Monica (contracts) to propose concrete options.

High level we usually run two paths: a) Short pilot billed consumption with a defined conversion credit applied to committed license fees if you convert within 90 days of pilot end, or b) Hybrid: a small upfront starter fee + consumption until an anchor commit is reached with the starter fee credited. Both preserve the ability to pin SLOs and include limited support during the pilot.

I'll kick off the internal thread and get you a clean one-page SOW + the conversion math by Wednesday. Would you prefer the credit be expressed as % of consumed spend or as an absolute $ per node/tokens?

Thanks — Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: On-prem inquiry — can we swap to consumption for pilot?

Team — forwarding Acme's ask (quote from Jason below). Need two tight options we can offer by EOD Monday for my call with their procurement on Tuesday. Keep numbers round but defensible.

Jason's ask: 6mo pilot, $75k spend cap, convert to multi-year on-prem license with a credit. He asked whether credit should be % of consumption or $/node/tokens.

Requirements for our response:
- Option A: Consumption-first, full platform & support included under cap, conversion credit expressed as % of pilot consumed spend when converting to a 1-2 year license. Show example math (e.g., $75k consumed -> 50% credit -> $37.5k applied to license).
- Option B: Starter-fee hybrid: small non-refundable starter (recommended $10k) + consumption under cap. Starter refundable as credit on conversion; conversion credit higher (e.g., 60-70% of total pilot spend including starter). This helps with risk.
- Support tiers: list limited pilot support (S0) vs production S1/S2 and add incremental fees.
- Any constraints/guardrails re: carrier nodes, KV cache persistence, and security add-ons for VPC must be explicit.

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (I attached an editable workbook with conversion scenarios), draft SOW template will be helpful too.

Diego

[Attachment: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: On-prem inquiry — can we swap to consumption for pilot?

Diego / team — see proposed two-option response below. I kept language customer-friendly and included an example conversion table so Acme can see the actual dollar math. Pulling any legal caveats from Monica/Olga afterward.

Option A — Consumption Pilot (no upfront):
- Pilot term: up to 6 months; gross spend cap: $75,000 (covers Redwood platform fee and pilot engineering support).
- Billing: monthly on consumption (per-inference unit).
- Conversion: If Acme converts to a 1-year on-prem license within 90 days of pilot completion, Redwood applies a credit equal to 50% of total pilot spend (cap $75k) against the first-year license invoice. Example: $75k consumed -> $37,500 credit.
- Support during pilot: Pilot S0 (1x weekly onboarding calls, 8x5 email support, incident triage only). Production S1/S2 available at added fees (see support table).
- Guardrails: KV cache persistence and long-term state not guaranteed in pilot; automated backups and extra security hardening are add-ons quoted separately.

Option B — Starter Fee + Consumption (risk-share):
- Starter fee: $10,000 due at SOW signing (applied as credit on conversion).
- Pilot consumption cap still $75k (starter is part of that cap).
- Conversion: If convert within 120 days, Redwood applies credit equal to starter fee + 60% of pilot consumption (up to $75k). Example: $10k starter + $30k consumed -> $10k + $18k = $28k credit.
- Support: includes elevated pilot support (S1-lite) with 24/7 paging for severity 1 during pilot.
- Guardrails: same as option A, plus we require a minimal node footprint (2 production-simulated nodes) to validate failover in pilot.

Support tiers (summary):
- Pilot S0: onboarding, 8x5 email support, 1 weekly sync.
- Pilot S1-lite: above + 24/7 paging for sev1, faster SLA for escalations.
- Prod S1: 24/7 coverage, designated tam, guaranteed response windows (SLA).

Attachments included for the email: sow_onprem_draft_v1.pdf (one-page pilot SOW draft) and support_tiers_summary.docx. I also filled the pricing scenarios into pricing_model_v3.xlsx — tab "ACME-pilot-scenarios" shows conversion math and the license-equivalent numbers.

Monica / Olga — any legal/contract language we should add for the conversion clause? Specifically: how to define "convert" (signed license + initial payment), and whether credits expire after X days. I'm proposing credits must be applied within 120 days of pilot completion.

-Marissa
Director, Pricing & Packaging
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: sow_onprem_draft_v1.pdf (pdf), support_tiers_summary.docx (docx), pricing_model_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Subject: Re: On-prem inquiry — consumption pilot + conversion credit (proposal)

Jason — thanks for the patience. Attaching a short SOW and two pricing options for the pilot (Option A: consumption-only with 50% credit on conversion; Option B: $10k starter + consumption with 60% credit on conversion). Key callouts below so legal/procurement can triage quickly.

Summary callouts:
- Pilot cap: $75,000 total spend (platform + support included).
- Conversion window: Credits valid if Acme executes a 1- or 2-year on-prem license within 120 days from pilot end. Credits applied to first-year invoice.
- Definition of conversion: signed license agreement + payment of first invoice (or agreed-upon initial invoice schedule).
- Support during pilot: Option A (Pilot S0), Option B (Pilot S1-lite). Production support tiers available thereafter.
- Security add-ons (VPC hardening, KMS integration) are billable outside of the pilot cap; we can include a time-and-materials not-to-exceed line in the SOW if you want these in-scope.

Next steps: please confirm which option Acme prefers and whether procurement wants the conversion credit expressed as % (we used %) or an absolute $ guarantee. If you confirm Option A or B, I'll route the SOW to legal for a quick DocuSign and share a draft link.

Warmly,
Diego Fernandez
